title: Missile strike on a cafe in Hroza, Kharkiv Oblast, kills dozens of civilians
body:
On 5 October 2023 a missile struck a cafe in the village of Hroza in Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, where residents had gathered for a wake. Local authorities said the missile appeared to be Russian. In a UN Human Rights briefing in Geneva on 6 October, spokesperson Liz Throssell said local authorities reported 52 people killed. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine had by then verified 27 deaths, 15 women and 12 men, and had recorded four injuries.

Authorities said one Ukrainian soldier who was attending his father's funeral was among those killed. The UN said at least eight families lost more than one relative. Hroza had about 300 residents before the Russian invasion, and it was unclear how many were still living there when the strike occurred. Throssell described the strike as one of the deadliest since 24 February 2022.

UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said he was profoundly shocked and condemned the attack, and he deployed a field team to the site to speak with survivors and gather information. The UN stressed that international humanitarian law, particularly the rules on the conduct of hostilities, must be strictly respected, and noted that the strike was far from the only one of its kind.
